symptoms.name: date-used-directly
symptoms.title: Date used directly
symptoms.seen: Any use of `Date` (`Date.now()`, `new Date()`, `new Date(value)`, `Date.parse`) or `performance.now()` outside the places that handle dates.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit that should be passed the time, often a doer doing two jobs

symptoms.name: ambient-randomness
symptoms.title: Ambient randomness
symptoms.seen: `Math.random()`, `crypto.randomUUID()` or `crypto.getRandomValues()` outside their adapter.

mayIndicate.case: Needs a random value or a new id

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit that should be passed the value, often a doer doing two jobs

correctUses.at: on the adapter for random values or new ids

symptoms.name: process-global-used-in-place
symptoms.title: Process global used in place
symptoms.seen: `process.env`, `process.argv`, `process.exit`, `process.on`, `console.*` or `globalThis` read outside an adapter.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: at a missing port, or at an adapter not built at the entry point

correctUses.at: on the adapter that wraps the process

symptoms.name: outside-import-past-a-boundary
symptoms.title: Outside import past a boundary
symptoms.seen: An import, `import()` or `require` of an outside dependency or runtime module (`node:*`) in a file with no boundary record.

mayIndicate.case: Uses a system or service outside the program

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: at a missing adapter and port

correctUses.at: on the adapter for that outside party

symptoms.name: outside-type-in-a-signature
symptoms.title: Outside type in a signature
symptoms.seen: A type from an outside dependency or runtime library in a business-logic parameter, field or return, imported or inferred.

mayIndicate.case: Uses a system or service outside the program

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the adapter that hands the outside type inward

correctUses.at: on the adapter, or beyond it with a Conformist statement for an outside model adopted as ours

symptoms.name: library-class-built-in-place
symptoms.title: Library class built in place
symptoms.seen: `new` on a class from an outside dependency, outside that dependency's adapter.

mayIndicate.case: Keeps state or settings across calls

symptoms.name: text-past-its-reader
symptoms.title: Text past its reader
symptoms.seen: `JSON.parse`, `JSON.stringify` or a YAML parse or dump outside the adapter for whoever produced or receives the text, tests included.

mayIndicate.case: Uses a system or service outside the program
States what the unit gives back

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in a port that takes or gives text where it should carry objects

correctUses.at: on the adapter for whoever produced or receives the text

correctUses.situation: a use at one test site

symptoms.name: schema-past-its-adapter
symptoms.title: Schema past its adapter
symptoms.seen: A schema, a `.parse` call or a `z.infer` type outside the producer's adapter, or the same value parsed twice.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the adapter, which hands the wire type inward instead of mapping it

correctUses.situation: an outside model adopted as ours

symptoms.name: claimed-type
symptoms.title: Claimed type
symptoms.seen: `as T` other than `as const`, `<T>x`, `x!` or `x!:`, including `as unknown` and any cast whose type holds `any`.

mayIndicate.case: Checks a value that may be one of several outcomes
Builds an input for a test with a cast

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the declaration: an input too wide, a generic not bounded, a missing parse

correctUses.at: in the adapter whose outside contract forces it

symptoms.name: untyped-value
symptoms.title: Untyped value
symptoms.seen: `any` in a type position, or a `let` with no type and no initial value.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: at the boundary that let an unknown shape in

symptoms.name: own-type-guard
symptoms.title: Own type guard
symptoms.seen: A function of ours whose return type is `x is T` or `asserts x is T`.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: at a missing schema parse in the adapter, or in a declaration too wide

symptoms.name: type-derived-from-code
symptoms.title: Type derived from code
symptoms.seen: `ReturnType<typeof x>`, `Parameters<typeof x>` or `typeof x` used as a type of our own.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the producer, which has no named type

correctUses.at: in the adapter for an outside dependency that gives no named type

symptoms.name: strictness-weakened
symptoms.title: Strictness weakened
symptoms.seen: A project whose resolved compiler options leave a strict flag off.

mayIndicate.case: Sets how strictly the checker works

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the base config or the project that overrides it

symptoms.name: default-on-a-closed-union
symptoms.title: Default on a closed union
symptoms.seen: `default:` in a `switch` over a closed union.

mayIndicate.case: A value is one of several kinds

symptoms.name: boolean-in-a-signature
symptoms.title: Boolean in a signature
symptoms.seen: A `boolean` parameter, field, or return that stands for a mode or state.

mayIndicate.case: A value is one of several kinds

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: at a missing named kind, or in a unit with two modes

symptoms.name: absence-standing-for-a-state
symptoms.title: Absence standing for a state
symptoms.seen: A field typed `T | null` or `T | undefined`, or optional, whose absence means a state rather than "not given".

mayIndicate.case: A value is one of several kinds

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the type, which needs named kinds

symptoms.name: default-for-a-required-value
symptoms.title: Default for a required value
symptoms.seen: `??`, `||` or a parameter default that supplies a required config, context or environment value.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the declaration or the adapter: a missing value is a failure

symptoms.name: throw-between-our-units
symptoms.title: Throw between our units
symptoms.seen: `throw` outside an adapter whose caller's contract is exceptions.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit, or at a missing mapping in the adapter

correctUses.at: at an adapter whose caller's contract is exceptions

symptoms.name: thrown-non-error
symptoms.title: Thrown non-error
symptoms.seen: `throw` of a literal, an object or a template.

symptoms.name: failure-shaped-as-success
symptoms.title: Failure shaped as success
symptoms.seen: A failed path that returns `null`, `false`, `[]`, `undefined` or a default, or a `catch` that returns one.

symptoms.name: catch-all-failure-kind
symptoms.title: Catch-all failure kind
symptoms.seen: A failure variant such as `unknown`, `other` or a bare message string, carrying no named cause.

mayIndicate.case: A value is one of several kinds

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the adapter, which did not name the outside failure

symptoms.name: loop-keyword
symptoms.title: Loop keyword
symptoms.seen: `for`, `for…of`, `for…in`, `for await`, `while` or `do`.

symptoms.name: write-into-a-parameter
symptoms.title: Write into a parameter
symptoms.seen: Assigning to or deleting a parameter's field, or calling an in-place method (`push`, `sort`, `splice`) on a parameter.

symptoms.name: rebinding
symptoms.title: Rebinding
symptoms.seen: A `let` assigned again, or a parameter reassigned, incremented or destructured into.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit: no caller sees it, so on its own it shows no hidden effect, but it is suspect for work done inline in steps

symptoms.name: authored-class-or-this
symptoms.title: Authored class or this
symptoms.seen: The `class` keyword in our code, `static`-only classes included, or `this` read outside a class.

mayIndicate.case: Keeps state or settings across calls

symptoms.name: module-level-state
symptoms.title: Module-level state
symptoms.seen: A module-scope `let`, or a module-scope collection that functions change.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: at a missing adapter for the state

symptoms.name: long-function
symptoms.title: Long function
symptoms.seen: A function body over the line limit.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit: several jobs, an input wider than its use, nested questions, or a responsibility not isolated and named

symptoms.name: tangled-function
symptoms.title: Tangled function
symptoms.seen: A function over the cognitive-complexity limit.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit: several jobs, an input wider than its use, nested questions, or a responsibility not isolated and named

symptoms.name: work-inside-a-condition
symptoms.title: Work inside a condition
symptoms.seen: An `if` inside another `if`, or an `else` after a branch that always exits.

symptoms.name: orchestrator-that-computes
symptoms.title: Orchestrator that computes
symptoms.seen: A function that calls two or more units of ours and also branches, computes or reshapes between the calls.

symptoms.name: doer-calling-our-own-unit
symptoms.title: Doer calling our own unit
symptoms.seen: A function with logic that imports and calls a business-logic unit of ours that is not a port.

mayIndicate.case: Uses what a collaborator gives back

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit, which mixes two roles

symptoms.name: positional-parameters
symptoms.title: Positional parameters
symptoms.seen: A function of ours, whose shape no outside API fixes, that has two or more parameters.

symptoms.name: tuple-as-data
symptoms.title: Tuple as data
symptoms.seen: An array literal or type of fixed mixed positions used as a value, such as `[key, value]` pairs or `pair[1]`.

symptoms.name: wide-input
symptoms.title: Wide input
symptoms.seen: A parameter type holding fields the unit never reads.

symptoms.name: wide-port
symptoms.title: Wide port
symptoms.seen: A port with methods its consumer never calls.

mayIndicate.case: Uses a system or service outside the program

symptoms.name: inner-layer-imports-outer
symptoms.title: Inner layer imports outer
symptoms.seen: A domain or business-logic file that imports an adapter or infrastructure file.

mayIndicate.case: Uses a system or service outside the program

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the import, or in a port declared on the wrong side

symptoms.name: port-outside-the-domain
symptoms.title: Port outside the domain
symptoms.seen: A port interface declared in an adapter's module, or beside its default adapter.

mayIndicate.case: Uses a system or service outside the program

symptoms.name: adapter-built-outside-the-root
symptoms.title: Adapter built outside the root
symptoms.seen: A call to an adapter's factory anywhere but the entry point.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the calling unit, which builds what it should be passed

symptoms.name: port-named-for-a-mechanism
symptoms.title: Port named for a mechanism
symptoms.seen: A port named for a technology (`HttpClient`, `Fs`, `Sqlite`) rather than a capability.

mayIndicate.case: Uses a system or service outside the program

symptoms.name: double-with-a-body
symptoms.title: Double with a body
symptoms.seen: A double that has a function body at all: `vi.fn(impl)`, `mockImplementation`, or a hand-written function or object double. A body that only returns a value is included.

mayIndicate.case: Uses what a collaborator gives back

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in a port too wide, or in a collaborator holding two decisions

correctUses.situation: a fake, where a stub cannot do the test

symptoms.name: module-or-global-patched
symptoms.title: Module or global patched
symptoms.seen: `vi.mock`, `vi.stubGlobal`, a spy on a global, or `process.env` set in a test.

mayIndicate.case: Uses what a collaborator gives back

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit, which imports what it should be passed

symptoms.name: branch-in-a-test
symptoms.title: Branch in a test
symptoms.seen: `if`, a ternary, `&&`, `||`, `??`, `?.` or `switch` in a test file.

mayIndicate.case: Checks a value that may be one of several outcomes

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit's output type, where optional or loose shapes force the test to branch

symptoms.name: computed-value-in-a-test
symptoms.title: Computed value in a test
symptoms.seen: A test that builds or picks a value: array methods, `find`, `Math.*`, `Object.assign`, `Object.fromEntries`, `Array.from` or a spread over a list. Calls on the unit's own API are not included.

mayIndicate.case: States what the unit gives back

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the test, or in logic no unit owns

symptoms.name: throw-or-catch-in-a-test
symptoms.title: Throw or catch in a test
symptoms.seen: `throw`, `try` or `catch` in a test file.

mayIndicate.case: States what the unit gives back

symptoms.name: unasserted-call
symptoms.title: Unasserted call
symptoms.seen: A stub or spy passed to the unit whose calls the test never asserts.

mayIndicate.case: Uses what a collaborator gives back

symptoms.name: answer-set-in-a-hook
symptoms.title: Answer set in a hook
symptoms.seen: A test hook that gives a stub its answer (`mockReturnValue`, `mockResolvedValue`, `mockImplementation`) or reassigns a value the tests read. A plain reset in `afterEach` is not this symptom.

mayIndicate.case: States what the unit gives back
Uses what a collaborator gives back

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in a double or a value shared across tests at file or suite scope, or in state held in the unit's module

symptoms.name: test-switched-off
symptoms.title: Test switched off
symptoms.seen: `.only`, `.skip`, `fit` or `xit`.

symptoms.name: unit-without-a-running-test
symptoms.title: Unit without a running test
symptoms.seen: A file with a runtime export and no `name.test.ts` beside it that imports and runs it.

symptoms.name: machine-touched-in-a-unit-test
symptoms.title: Machine touched in a unit test
symptoms.seen: A unit test that reads or writes files, spawns a process, opens a socket or makes a temp directory.

mayIndicate.case: Tests across units or against a real system
Uses what a collaborator gives back

symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the unit, which has no port, or in a test that is an integration test misnamed

symptoms.name: inherited-environment-in-a-subprocess
symptoms.title: Inherited environment in a subprocess
symptoms.seen: A process spawned in a test with no explicit environment, or one built from `process.env`.

mayIndicate.case: Tests across units or against a real system

symptoms.name: behaviour-tested-away-from-its-owner
symptoms.title: Behaviour tested away from its owner
symptoms.seen: A unit test that asserts what a collaborator does, or an integration test that pins a rule a unit owns.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the level the test is written at

symptoms.name: integration-heavy-suite
symptoms.title: Integration-heavy suite
symptoms.seen: More integration tests, or more integration test cases, than the bindings to the outside they cover.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in missing unit tests and ports

symptoms.name: coverage-gate
symptoms.title: Coverage gate
symptoms.seen: A coverage percentage threshold in test config.

symptoms.name: large-input-for-a-few-fields
symptoms.title: Large input for a few fields
symptoms.seen: A test that writes a large object, or casts, to give the unit the few fields it reads.

symptoms.name: test-of-the-type-checker
symptoms.title: Test of the type checker
symptoms.seen: A test that asserts only what the types already prove, such as exhaustiveness.

symptoms.name: shorthand-name
symptoms.title: Shorthand name
symptoms.seen: A name of single letters, an abbreviation or a filler word (`data`, `result`, `options`, `tx`), at any scope.

correctUses.situation: a name an outside contract fixes

symptoms.name: name-off-its-casing
symptoms.title: Name off its casing
symptoms.seen: An identifier or file name outside the adopter's casing convention.

correctUses.situation: an outside contract's names, such as `PATH` or ESLint listener keys

symptoms.name: drawer-path
symptoms.title: Drawer path
symptoms.seen: A file or folder named utils, helpers, types, common, shared or the like.

mayIndicate.case: Puts code in a file or folder

symptoms.name: types-only-file
symptoms.title: Types-only file
symptoms.seen: A file that declares only types and is not a port declaration.

symptoms.name: prose-in-code
symptoms.title: Prose in code
symptoms.seen: Any comment or JSDoc other than a tracked pointer or a covered tool directive.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in a name or type that does not carry the meaning

symptoms.name: untracked-escape
symptoms.title: Untracked escape
symptoms.seen: A TODO, linter directive or `@ts-*` directive with no tracked reference and no record.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: in the record that is missing, and in whatever rule the directive switches off

symptoms.name: many-spellings-of-one-concept
symptoms.title: Many spellings of one concept
symptoms.seen: One domain concept named two or more ways across the code or the wire.

symptoms.name: outside-dependency-vocabulary-for-basic-logic
symptoms.title: Outside dependency vocabulary for basic logic
symptoms.seen: An import of a utility or functional outside dependency (lodash, fp-ts) for branching, matching, transforming or results.

symptoms.name: duplicate-decision
symptoms.title: Duplicate decision
symptoms.seen: The same decision written in two or more places.
symptoms.breachUsuallySits: where the decision's home should be; a clone only surfaces a candidate

symptoms.name: change-spread-across-modules
symptoms.title: Change spread across modules
symptoms.seen: One change for one reason touches many modules, or two modules always change together.

symptoms.name: floating-version
symptoms.title: Floating version
symptoms.seen: A range (`^`, `~`, `*`, `x`) or a tag (`latest`, `lts`) for an outside dependency, a runtime or a CI action.

symptoms.name: no-lock-file
symptoms.title: No lock file
symptoms.seen: A repository with dependencies and no committed lock file.

symptoms.name: dependency-without-a-record
symptoms.title: Dependency without a record
symptoms.seen: A direct dependency, tools included, with no record of the native way weighed.

correctUses.at: naming the native way weighed and why it fell short

symptoms.name: tool-fetched-at-run-time
symptoms.title: Tool fetched at run time
symptoms.seen: `npx`, `dlx`, `bunx` or a download-and-run in a script, CI step or doc.

symptoms.name: edit-inside-vendored-code
symptoms.title: Edit inside vendored code
symptoms.seen: A change to a file inside a vendored folder.

correctUses.situation: drift, an edit impossible to apply as an extension

symptoms.name: bundled-dependency
symptoms.title: Bundled dependency
symptoms.seen: Published build output that holds a dependency's code that the package manifest does not declare.
